thread.title: Stifel remains bullish on Applied Materials, sees buying opportunity AMAT;MKSI - The Fly

title: Stifel remains bullish on Applied Materials, sees buying opportunity AMAT;MKSI - The Fly
text:
On The Fly: Top stock stories for Tuesday » Stocks began the day deep… 
Stocks began the day deep in negative territory and tacked on additional losses throughout the session. Concern over the potential shortcoming of the Apple (AAPL) iPhone "supercycle" and the potential disruption in the healthcare market from the joint venture between Amazon (AMZN), Berkshire (BRK.A) and JP Morgan (JPM) had roiled investors who chose to take profits with the market at record highs. The two-day losing streak is the market's first this year and comes ahead of tonight's State of the Union address from President Trump. ECONOMIC EVENTS: In the U.S., the Case-Shiller 20-city home price index rose 0.25% to 204.21 in November. The Conference Board's consumer confidence index increased to 125.4 in January, following a decline to 123.1 in December. In Europe, the Eurozone advance GDP number for the three months through December 2017 pointed to growth of 0.6%, in-line with consensus, while Eurozone confidence numbers for January fell a bit short of expectations. COMPANY NEWS: Amazon, Berkshire Hathaway and JPMorgan announced a partnership to better address healthcare for their U.S. employees. The news sent shares of the owners of pharmacy benefit managers, including Express Scripts (ESRX), CVS Health (CVS) and UnitedHealth (UNH), into negative territory and also weighed broadly on health insurers, including Aetna (AET), Anthem (ANTM), Centene (CNC), Cigna (CI), Humana (HUM) and WellCare (WCG)... McDonald's (MCD) dipped 3% after reporting its global comparable sales increased 5.3%, including a 4.5% increase in the U.S., in the fourth quarter... Shares of Pfizer (PFE) declined 3% despite the drugmaker reporting fourth quarter results that beat consensus expectations and providing better than expected guidance for fiscal 2018. The company added that it is on track to explore decisions for its Consumer Healthcare business during 2018... Meanwhile, Apple shares slipped about 0.6% after Bloomberg reported that the U.S. Department of Justice and Securities and Exchange Commission are investigating whether the U.S. tech giant violated securities laws concerning its disclosures about a software update that slowed older iPhone models. The U.S. government has requested information from the company, and the inquiry in in the early stages, according to Bloomberg. MAJOR MOVERS: Among the noteworthy gainers was Achaogen (AKAO), which rose 10% after it said that the FDA has classified the outcome of its fourth quarter 2017 reinspection of Pfizer's McPherson facility as Voluntary Action Indicated, or VAI, thus providing a "clear regulatory path" for the approval of plazomicin out of that facility. Also higher was Callidus Software (CALD), which gained 10% after it agreed to be acquired by SAP (SAP) for $36 per share. Among the notable losers after reporting quarterly results were Scotts Miracle-Gro (SMG), Harley-Davidson (HOG), and AK Steel (AKS). Also lower was Parsley Energy (PE), which slid 14% after the stock saw several downgrades following the company's announcement of production guidance. INDEXES: The Dow fell 362.59, or 1.37%, to 26,076.89, the Nasdaq lost 64.02, or 0.86%, to 7,402.48, and the S&P 500 declined 31.10, or 1.09%, to 2,822.43. AAPL
